content.title: About
content.content: Bread is a staple food made by baking dough from flour, water, yeast and salt. Egg is the nutrient‑rich reproductive part of birds, widely used in cooking. Challah is a traditional Jewish braided loaf, prepared from a yeasted dough enriched with eggs, oil and sometimes honey.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bread has been made for over 10,000 years; the earliest forms were simple flatbreads baked on open fires.
Eggs are an almost perfect protein source, containing all essential amino acids in optimal ratios.
Challah is traditionally baked for Shabbat and holidays; its braiding symbolizes the intertwining of family bonds.
In many cultures bread is a symbol of life and prosperity, and a slice of bread is often used in greeting rituals.
Unwashed eggs can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 weeks.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Bread and challah provide quick‑release carbohydrates, while eggs deliver high‑quality protein for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain bread and eggs are rich in B1, B2, B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Eggs contain iron, phosphorus and selenium; challah often gains extra calcium and magnesium from added dairy.

items.title: Choline
items.content: Eggs are one of the best dietary sources of choline, essential for brain health and liver function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain bread and challah made with whole‑meal flour supply dietary fiber that aids regular digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals develop an allergy to egg white proteins, which can cause skin reactions up to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: Wheat‑based bread contains gluten, which may cause problems for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Commercial breads often contain high levels of salt; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Cholesterol
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol; those with elevated cholesterol levels should moderate egg intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw or undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella; it is important to cook eggs thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bread can be eaten fresh, toasted, as sandwiches, or used in soups and casseroles. Eggs are boiled, fried, made into omelets, pâtés and incorporated into baked goods. Challah is served as a festive loaf, often sliced and spread with butter or honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bread and challah in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days; for longer storage keep them in a sealed container in the refrigerator (up to 7 days). Keep eggs in their original carton in the fridge, where they stay fresh for up to 5 weeks.
